cards.text: Paul's on trial again, friend, and this time he's standing in front of King Agrippa. Agrippa says, "You have permission to speak for yourself." Paul stretches out his hand like a man who's been waiting ALL WEEK for somebody to pass him the mic.

cards.question: Paul opens his defense before King Agrippa. How does Paul say he feels about standing before the king today?

answers.text: He feels he's been treated unfairly
He's afraid of what the king will decide

cards.question: Paul is defending himself against accusations from the Jews. Why is he especially glad that King Agrippa is the one hearing it?

answers.text: The king knows Jewish customs well
The king owes Paul a favor
The king has already freed him once

cards.text: Then Paul tells the king, "I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently." Translation: get comfy, Your Majesty, this one's got CHAPTERS.

cards.question: Paul says the Jews have known how he's lived since his earliest childhood. He lived as a ___, in the strictest sect of their religion.

cards.text: Now Paul gets to the charge itself. He says he's on trial because of his hope in the promise God made to their fathers.

cards.question: Paul says only a few faithful people are still hoping to see God's promise to their fathers fulfilled.
Paul is on trial over his hope in God's promise. He turns to the whole room with a question. What does he say none of them should find incredible?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth." Friend, the man on trial just started reading his OWN rap sheet out loud. On purpose.

cards.question: Back in Jerusalem, Paul had authority from the chief priests. What does he say he used it to do?

answers.text: Put many of the saints in prison
Guard the treasury of the temple
Collect taxes from the people for Rome

cards.question: When the saints in Jerusalem were condemned to death, Paul says he cast his vote against them.

cards.text: And Paul keeps going. He says he frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and he tried to make them blaspheme.

cards.question: Paul says he was in a raging fury against the saints. Where did he even go to persecute them?

cards.text: That's what Paul was doing on his way to Damascus, carrying the authority and commission of the chief priests. Paperwork signed, plan locked in, and I bet not one doubt in his head.

cards.question: About noon, Paul is on the road to Damascus. What does he see shining around him and his companions?

answers.text: A light from heaven brighter than the sun
A pillar of fire stretched across the road
An angel standing in the middle of their path

cards.text: They all fall to the ground, and Paul hears a voice speaking to him in Hebrew. Friend, I lived in a dark drawer for YEARS, and if a light brighter than the noon sun showed up, I wouldn't just fall down, I'd ROLL.

cards.question: On the ground, Paul hears a voice say to him in Hebrew, 'Saul, Saul.' What does the voice ask him?

answers.text: Where do you think you're going

cards.question: The voice on the Damascus road tells Saul that it's easy for him to kick against the goads.

cards.text: So Paul asks the only question that makes sense when you're lying in the dirt at noon: "Who are You, Lord?"

cards.question: On the Damascus road, Paul tells the king: "I am ___, whom you are persecuting," the Lord replied.

cards.text: Then the Lord tells him, "But get up and stand on your feet." Saul set out to persecute Jesus' people, and now Jesus is about to hand him a whole new assignment.

cards.question: On the Damascus road, Jesus tells Saul why He appeared to him. What is He appointing Saul to be?
Jesus tells Saul He will rescue him from his own people and from the Gentiles.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He's sending Saul to them, to open their eyes. The man who was just flat on the ground is now in charge of opening EYES. Friend, that's what you call a career change.

cards.question: Jesus is sending Saul to open people's eyes. What does Jesus want them to turn from and turn to?

answers.text: From the city to the desert

cards.question: When people turn from the power of Satan to God, what does Jesus say they will receive?

answers.text: Forgiveness of sins and an inheritance
Long life and a land of their own
Great riches and a seat of honor

cards.text: Paul tells the king, "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision." He started in Damascus and Jerusalem, then all of Judea, then the Gentiles.

cards.question: From Damascus all the way to the Gentiles, what did Paul declare that people should do?
Paul taught that people's repentance should show up in the things they do.

cards.text: For this reason, Paul says, the Jews seized him in the temple courts and tried to kill him. But he's had God's help to this day, and here he stands, testifying to small and great alike.

cards.question: Paul says he's saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen. What did they say about the Christ?

answers.text: He would suffer and rise first from the dead
He would conquer Rome with a mighty army
He would rule forever without ever suffering

cards.question: Paul says the Christ would proclaim light only to the people of Israel.

cards.text: Right at this point in Paul's defense, Festus, the governor, can't hold it in anymore. He doesn't raise his hand. He just YELLS.

cards.question: Festus interrupts Paul's defense in a loud voice. What does Festus call Paul?
Festus shouts that something is driving Paul to madness. What does Festus blame?

cards.text: Paul answers, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety." Friend, the man gets called crazy in front of a KING and still opens with MOST EXCELLENT.

cards.question: Paul turns back to King Agrippa. Why is Paul confident none of this has escaped the king's notice?

answers.text: None of it happened in a corner
The king saw the light himself
The king read the priests' letters

cards.text: Then Paul asks him straight out, "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do." He asked AND answered, like a text that says "You coming tonight? You're coming."

cards.question: Paul just asked King Agrippa if he believes the prophets. How does the king answer Paul?

answers.text: He asks if Paul can make him a Christian that fast
He says he gave up on the prophets long ago
He tells the guards to take Paul away right now

cards.text: Paul says, "Short time or long," and then he tells the king what he wishes to God for everyone in that room.

cards.question: Paul wishes the king and everyone who hears him would become what he is, except for these ___.

cards.text: Then the king and the governor rise, along with Bernice, who came in with the king, and everyone seated with them. When a king stands up, friend, the meeting is OVER.

cards.question: On their way out, the king and the others agree that Paul has done something worthy of imprisonment.
After hearing Paul's defense, what does King Agrippa tell Festus about Paul?

answers.text: He could have been freed if he hadn't appealed to Caesar
He should be sent back to Jerusalem to face his accusers
He should stay locked up in Caesarea for the rest of his life

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 7 quotes "I am ___, whom you are persecuting", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The included sermon Acts 26:2-23 doesn't have a stop of its own covering exactly those verses.

rule.text: An included parable or sermon (see passages.md) gets a stop of its own.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Where did he even go to persecute them?' The word 'even' signals somewhere beyond the usual, which rules out the wrong answer 'Only Jerusalem' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The drawer joke ('if a light brighter than the noon sun showed up, I wouldn't just fall down, I'd ROLL') does not click. 'I'd ROLL' needs explaining. It also blends the Bible setting (the noon sun) into the drawer comparison. And in his backstory a bright light did come into the drawer, and he only blinked up at it, so the 'what if' framing works against what bakers already know.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Where do you think you're going' is a modern, casual phrase. The right answer 'Why do you persecute Me' has a Bible tone, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Paul tells the king:' and then quotes 'I am ___', so the 'I' first reads as Paul. The Lord is named as the speaker only at the end. This makes it unclear who is speaking.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The joke 'The man who was just flat on the ground is now in charge of opening EYES' has no contrast that clicks, because lying on the ground has nothing to do with opening eyes. It also repeats the 'new assignment' idea from card 8.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 7 of the stop's 12 choice cards. There are 3 true or false cards and only 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the stop's 7 choice cards. There is only 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'Festus... can't hold it in anymore' states a feeling as fact. The text only says Festus 'exclaimed in a loud voice.'

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The right answer 'He asks if Paul can make him a Christian that fast' changes Agrippa's word 'persuade' (Acts 26:28) to 'make.' Those mean different things.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the last word of Paul's line ('except for these ___'). No earlier card says Paul is in chains or a prisoner, so the baker is guessing wording they haven't seen rather than reasoning out the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'Bernice, who came in with the king' is a fact from outside the passage (Acts 25:23), but the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Acts 26:30.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
